headlines.title: How Dr Pepper’s ‘Fansville’ campaign stays relevant and drives outcomes
headlines.summary: Keurig Dr Pepper marketer Derek Dabrowski digs into how the college football campaign, now in its ninth season, is lifting sales through personalization.

headlines.title: Can Keurig Dr Pepper's Energy Growth Offset Coffee Market Softness?
headlines.summary: KDP's fast-rising energy portfolio is nearing double-digit share as U.S. Coffee battles weaker sales, shipments and higher costs.

headlines.title: The 5 Most Interesting Analyst Questions From Keurig Dr Pepper’s Q2 Earnings Call
headlines.summary: Keurig Dr Pepper’s second quarter was marked by robust revenue growth, powered by the successful integration of JDE Peet’s and continued strength in U.S. Refreshment Beverages. Management credited double-digit sales gains in carbonated soft drinks, energy, and sports hydration as key drivers, with new launches like Dr Pepper Zero Sugar and Bloom Pop contributing to share gains.

headlines.title: Did New 7UP Formula, Dr Pepper Shakes and Board Addition Just Shift Keurig Dr Pepper's (KDP) Investment Narrative?
headlines.summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has recently reported second-quarter 2026 results showing sales of US$7.31 billion and net income of US$142 million, while rolling out a lime-led reformulation of 7UP and partnering with Portillo’s on limited-time Dr Pepper shakes in the U.S. Alongside these product moves, the company has added Cardinal Health CFO Aaron Alt to its board as it works through a planned split into separate beverage and coffee businesses.

description: Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. owns, manufactures, and distributors beverages and single serve brewing systems in the United States and internationally. The company operates through three segments: U.S. Refreshment Beverages, U.S. Coffee, and International. It manufactures and distributes branded concentrates, syrup, and finished beverages, as well as sales of owned brands and third-party brands; tea, cocoa, and other products; and offers finished goods relating to K-Cup pods, single serve brewers, specialty coffee, and ready to drink coffee products. The company offers its products under the Dr Pepper, Canada Dry, Mott's, A&W, Peñafiel, GHOST, Snapple, 7UP, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, Clamato, Core Hydration, The Original Donut Shop, Sunkist soda, Squirt, C4 Energy, Hawaiian Punch, Electrolit, Bloom, Bai, Evian, Yoo-Hoo, Vita Coco, Big Red, RC Cola, Crush, McCafé, Tim Hortons, Van Houtte, Celestial Seasonings, Bigelow, Starbucks, Dunkin', Folgers, Peet's, and Swiss Miss brands, as well as other partner and private label brands. It markets and sells its products to supermarkets, mass merchandisers, club stores, e-commerce retailers, office superstores, vending machines, fountains, grocery and drug stores, convenience stores, and other small outlets; and directly to consumers through Keurig.com website. Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. was founded in 1981 and is headquartered in Frisco, Texas.
